messages:
Alice: paging — customers in EU are seeing 429s on /v1/generate since ~10:05 UTC. Error spike looks correlated with a rollout earlier today. Can we triage?

Ben: I'm on it, looking at ingress metrics now. Saw a sudden jump in queue depth for nodepool-gpu-a.

Caroline: alerted SDKs and asked for any client-side patterns. Any evidence of aggressive retry loops?

Ben: some clients are hammering after transient 503s. We already have a circuit-breaker but it's per-connection and some older SDKs don't set idempotency keys.

oncall-bot: Incident created: INC-2026-314 — 429 surge affecting EU region. Pager sent to oncall rotation.

Alice: immediate mitigation proposal (short window): 1) soft rate-limit consumer tier to 150rps per-token across EU edge 2) raise dedicated quota for critical partners by 2x 3) toggle feature-flag to disable real-time reranker (non-critical) 4) ask SDK owners to back off retries + add jitter. Thoughts?

Ben: agree. I'm going to patch the ingress shaper now to apply a temporary global token-bucket for anonymous traffic: 
```
rictl traffic shape set --region=eu --policy=soft-throttle --rate=150rps --burst=500
```
Applying in 2m.

Caroline: I'll draft a short note for SDKs. Key asks: reduce retry multiplier and add jitter; switch to exponential backoff with cap 20s; avoid immediate retry on 429s. Sample guidance coming.

Alice: also enabling quick quota bump for a handful of enterprise customers that reported impact. Ben, can you whitelist partner keys?

Ben: doing whitelist patch: 
```
rictl quota adjust --key=partner-ACME --rate=600rps --region=eu --note="temp bump for mitigation"
```
Whitelisted keys: partner-ACME, partner-Bytewell. Changes live in 30s.

Caroline: posting SDK guidance draft — please copy/paste into engineering status channel and into customer-facing support template.

Caroline: "SDK mitigation steps (copyable):
1) Immediately stop immediate retry loops. If you see a 429 or 503, wait before retrying.
2) Recommended retry algorithm: exponential backoff with full jitter — base=300ms, factor=2.0, max=20s. Example pseudocode:
```
function nextDelay(attempt) {\n  const base = 300;\n  const factor = 2.0;\n  const max = 20000; // ms\n  const raw = Math.min(max, base * Math.pow(factor, attempt));\n  return Math.random() * raw; // full jitter\n}
```
3) Prefer idempotency keys for non-idempotent endpoints to avoid duplicated work. Use UUID v4 and attach header `X-Redwood-Idempotency`.
4) Honor Retry-After header and implement a client side circuit breaker: 5xx/429 rate > 50% over 30s should open breaker for 10s.
5) Reduce parallelism: cap concurrent inflight requests per process to 6 by default.

Note: We'll ship a patch to official SDKs to opt-in these defaults within 2 hours. If you maintain a fork, apply these changes ASAP."

Ben: ingress shaping applied. Observability shows immediate drop in incoming RPS from anonymous clients. 429 rate across EU service dropped from 12% -> 4% in first 60s.

Alice: good. I'm going to disable reranker FF now — non-essential for accuracy and high cost. Toggle command: 
```
rictl feature toggle --name=reranker-real-time --env=prod --state=off --region=eu --reason="mitigation"
```

oncall-bot: Feature flag "reranker-real-time" set to OFF by Alice at 2026-07-12T10:12:10Z

Caroline: pushing SDK hotfix branch with default retry/jitter and idempotency header helper. PR: https://git.redwood.ai/sdk/pulls/748 (draft). Will mark as critical patch.

Ben: monitoring logs — backend latency also decreased which suggests less queueing and fewer hot-shard evictions.

Alice: coordination for handoff — Ben, you stay primary for next 30m. Caroline, please watch SDK PR and support app teams. I'll update support & status page. If 429s stay <5% for 20m, we'll start rolling back non-critical mitigations (reranker + whitelists) one by one.

Caroline: support template ready — short version for customer comms: 
"We observed elevated rate limiting in EU due to an automated rollout + retry storms. We applied temporary rate shaping and increased partner quotas. Recommended client action: upgrade SDK or implement exponential backoff with jitter; use idempotency keys for retries. We will notify when fully resolved."

Ben: logs look stable. 15m into mitigation, legacy clients still producing spikes — recommend a server-side soft header to signal clients to back off: add 'X-Rate-Limit-Advice: jitter' and HTTP 429 body with suggested backoff. I can add quick middleware.

Alice: do it. Also create a short-lived rollout to nudge client libs: bump default backoff multiplier on the CDN edge for JS SDKs to 1.5.

Ben: middleware in place. Example response body we will send for 429s to unauthenticated calls:
```
{ "error": "rate_limit", "advice": "use exponential backoff with jitter; suggested base_ms=300; max_ms=20000" }
```

oncall-bot: INC-2026-314 status: mitigation in progress; next update in 15m.

Caroline: SDK PR merged to main with hotfix and release note. Publishing patch release 1.4.3 now. Changelog includes: default retry with full jitter, idempotency helper, lowered default concurrency for browser SDK.

Alice: great. plan for rollback: 1) confirm 429 < 1% for 30m 2) re-enable reranker FF 3) remove anonymous soft-throttle and keep partner quotas restored 4) follow-up postmortem and action items for rollout gating and canary throttling.

Ben: metrics tell us to hold for another 20m, but things look good. I'll document exact commands used in the incident playbook.

Caroline: outreach to top 5 impacted customers sent. They acknowledged and will patch clients overnight.

Alice: thanks all. If anything regresses, escalate immediately and we re-open the page. I'll file the post-incident ticket and include SDK owners for follow-up on idempotency adoption and better client-side defaults.

Ben: logging final note: created postmortem ticket PM-2026-98 and assigned to infra-team; will include timeline, metrics, and suggested CI gating for model rollouts.

oncall-bot: INC-2026-314: mitigation reached steady state at 2026-07-12T10:45:00Z — monitoring.

Alice: closing thread for now, will update when we start rollback. Thanks everyone :heart:
